title: The Powerplay Equation: When Sunrisers Hyderabad Should Attack the First Six Overs
dek: How fast should Sunrisers Hyderabad start? Ball-by-ball data shows the first six overs reward runs, but punish lost wickets even more.
excerpt: Sunrisers Hyderabad have been ahead of the league's powerplay scoring rate since 2024. Across every IPL innings, an early wicket costs more win probability than a quick start earns.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: The First Six Overs, Measured
body: Every T20 innings starts with the same bargain: two fielders outside the circle, a new ball, and a choice about risk. For Sunrisers Hyderabad the record shows how that bargain has been struck. Between 2013 and 2023 the side scored at {{ev:pp-team-e1}} runs per over in the powerplay while the league scored at {{ev:pp-league-e1}}, which put them behind the average.

Since 2024 the scoring environment has changed for everyone. SRH have scored at {{ev:pp-team-e2}} in the powerplay against a league figure of {{ev:pp-league-e2}}, ahead of the pace of the competition. Across the seasons in the CricField warehouse they finished above the league's powerplay rate in {{ev:pp-good-seasons}} of {{ev:pp-season-count}}.
On this measure their strongest season was 2024, at {{ev:pp-x-best-v}}, and their weakest 2013, at {{ev:pp-x-worst-v}}.

sections.heading: What a Powerplay Wicket Costs
body: Runs are only half of the equation. Grouping every IPL innings with a result by wickets lost in the first six overs gives a steep staircase: sides that kept all ten wickets won {{ev:ppw-l0}} of the time, sides two down won {{ev:ppw-l2}}, and sides three or more down won {{ev:ppw-l3}}. The steepest single step is worth {{ev:ppw-stepmax}} percentage points of win rate.
Sunrisers Hyderabad's own {{ev:ppw-tinn}} innings with a result follow the same pattern: {{ev:ppw-t0}} with no powerplay wickets lost, {{ev:ppw-t3}} with three or more.

sections.heading: Who Carries the Risk
body: Among SRH's recent openers, {{ev:ppb-lead-name}} faced the most powerplay balls since 2024, {{ev:ppb-lead-balls}} of them, at a strike rate of {{ev:ppb-lead-sr}}.

The useful question for selectors is not whether to attack but who absorbs the risk. The player table shows each recent powerplay batter's strike rate beside how many balls they survive per dismissal; a pairing works when at least one of the two keeps the wicket count low while the other accelerates.

sections.heading: The Case for Swinging Harder
body: The league has sped up, and deeper batting line-ups since the impact-player rule may make an early wicket cheaper than the long-run averages suggest. The full-history staircase mixes eras in which a collapse was harder to absorb.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Price the Wicket First
body: Sunrisers Hyderabad should keep pace with a faster league, but the evidence says the binding constraint in the powerplay is wickets. Across the IPL, a start of fifty-odd for one or fewer has won {{ev:pp-steady}} of the time, while sixty-plus for two or more has won {{ev:pp-reckless}}: the steadier start wins more often.
The practical rule is one licensed attacker and one risk-absorber at the top, chosen on balls per dismissal as much as on strike rate.

methodology: Regulation innings only (super overs excluded). Run rates use all runs per legal ball times six. Every figure is generated from the CricField warehouse by scripts/editorial/engine. Powerplay = overs one to six. Wickets exclude retired hurt. Player table: balls faced exclude wides.
